evidence: packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256 and 315-317: the find() fallback runs only when externalCalendarId is falsy, then compares cal.externalId === externalCalendarId (null/undefined/''). DestinationCalendar.externalId is a non-null string, so find() always returns undefined. updateEvent passes calendarId: selectedCalendar (undefined) to events.update (line 261); deleteEvent falls back to 'primary' (line 322). Before the PR both used event.destinationCalendar.externalId, so this is a regression for references with no externalCalendarId. Fix: fall back to the destination matching this credential (as createEvent does) or to the first entry.

packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:221 declares createEvent(event, credentialId). packages/app-store/larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:125 declares createEvent(event). TypeScript parameter bivariance/arity rules let an implementation with fewer parameters satisfy an interface method with more, so this does not break the contract or the build. Office365 and the base CalDAV service also leave the parameter off. The real issue is routing (see #2), not the type contract.

larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128 (createEvent) and :164 (createAttendees) use destinationCalendar[0] unconditionally. EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents (packages/core/EventManager.ts:338-380) calls createEvent once per destination with that host's credential, so a secondary host's Lark credential would target the main host's calendar id. That part is valid. Lines 192 and 237 (update/delete) use externalCalendarId from the booking reference first and only fall back to [0], so the claim is overstated for those two. Fix: pick the destination by credentialId, like Google's createEvent does (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:147-149).

packages/core/EventManager.ts:118-119: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` gives undefined when the array is null or empty, and then `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` is read with no optional chaining. Because of the && short-circuit this only runs when evt.location === MeetLocationType, which is exactly the Meet-without-Google-Calendar case the Daily fallback is for. That case now throws a TypeError instead of switching to integrations:daily. handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 can set destinationCalendar to null, and other callers pass []. Before the PR the code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`. Fix: `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

EventManager.ts:338-380 loops over destinations but calls createEvent(credential, event, destination.externalId). CalendarManager.createEvent (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:218-268) only copies externalId into the result and passes the whole event plus credential.id to the provider. Only Google (googlecalendar CalendarService.ts:147-149) picks its destination by credentialId. Office365 (office365calendar CalendarService.ts:73-77), Lark (:128) and the base CalDAV service (packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156-164) all use destinationCalendar[0], so they target the first host's calendar id with the other host's credential. That causes 404s, or for CalDAV the filter matches no calendar, so secondary hosts get no event.

EventManager.ts:511-542: if reference.credentialId matches neither this.calendarCredentials nor a DB credential with app.slug, credential stays undefined and updateEvent(credential, ...) is still pushed. BookingReference.credentialId is a plain Int? with no FK (packages/prisma/schema.prisma:342), so stale ids can happen. CalendarManager.updateEvent survives getCalendar(undefined), which returns null, but then reads credential.appName (CalendarManager.ts:314), so the promise rejects. The mechanism in the comment is wrong, though. EventManager.ts:588 does `return Promise.all(result)` without await inside the try, so the rejection skips the catch at 589-608 and rejects the whole updateAllCalendarEvents call, which is arguably worse. The behaviour predates the PR (the old filter()[0] could also be undefined), but the per-reference loop makes it more likely. Fix: skip or return a failure entry for that reference.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:418-485: inside the new per-reference loop, the recurring branch ignores the current reference. It loops over bookingToDelete.user.credentials and, for each updBooking, uses updBooking.references.find(ref => ref.type.includes('_calendar')), which is only the first calendar reference. With N host references, the first host's events get deleted repeatedly (N x credentials times) and other hosts' events are never deleted. The branch also uses bookingToDelete.user.credentials instead of the calendarCredential fetched from the DB at 430-439, so team members' credentials are not used.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067 sets destinationCalendar to null when neither eventType nor organizerUser has one. Lines 1077-1079 run `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`, which does nothing on null. A collective event where only the non-organizer hosts have destination calendars therefore ends up with no destinations, and EventManager falls back to the credential-iteration path for the organizer only. Fix: initialise to [] or assign `[...(evt.destinationCalendar ?? []), ...teamDestinationCalendars]`.

The interface part is invalid: packages/lib/CalendarService.ts createEvent(event) with fewer parameters is assignable to Calendar.createEvent(event, credentialId) in TypeScript (see #1). The routing part is valid: lines 156-164 filter this credential's calendars by mainHostDestinationCalendar.externalId, the first host's CalDAV URL. For a secondary collective host's credential that URL won't match any of their calendars, so no event is created for them. Fix: pick the destination by credentialId.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151-153: the PR changed `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`, which flips the logic. Billing-enabled orgs now get both slug and requestedSlug, and billing-disabled orgs get neither. The publish flow (organizations/publish.handler.ts:68) sets slug from requestedSlug after payment, so setting slug early skips the pending state. This is an unrelated regression in a calendar PR. Restore `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` for slug.

office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:94 updateEvent(uid, event) and :111 deleteEvent(uid) omit trailing parameters. That is legal TypeScript and not a contract violation. They call /me/calendar/events/{uid} (lines 96, 113), which ignores externalCalendarId while createEvent (line 76) posts to /me/calendars/{id}/events. In Microsoft Graph, event ids are unique per mailbox and /me/events/{id} resolves across calendars, but the /me/calendar/ (default calendar) path can fail for events in other calendars. The concern is plausible but predates the PR (these lines are untouched), so it is out of scope here.

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/requestReschedule.handler.ts:240-242: bookingToReschedule comes from findFirstOrThrow (line 43), so it is never nullish and both `?.` are redundant. The surrounding code uses `bookingToReschedule?.uid` and `?.location` the same way (lines 238-239), so this matches local style and has no runtime effect. It is a nitpick.
